researcher_notes: Fresh re-check of the 8 honest 'unknown' positions from dataset_v1 (snapshot 2026-05-14), focused exclusively on primary-source statements made between 2026-05-14 and 2026-05-21. Searched: (a) each candidate's campaign website news / priorities pages (xavierbecerra2026.com/news, /priorities; katieporter.com/news, /priorities; tonythurmond.com/in-the-news, /priorities); (b) coverage of the final pre-primary debate on 2026-05-14 (CBS Bay Area / SF Examiner) via SF Standard, CalMatters, SFist, and PBS NewsHour writeups; (c) post-debate interviews including the SD City Times Becerra introduction (2026-05-15), ABC7 Porter sit-down (2026-05-17), KEYT/News Channel 3-12 Thurmond profile (2026-05-15); (d) candidate forum coverage (CalMatters, Black Voice News, Capitol Weekly); (e) major outlets (CalMatters, KQED, LA Times, SF Chronicle, Sac Bee, EdSource); (f) Thurmond's 2026-05-14 statement on the May Revise budget (as Superintendent — addressed K-12 funding, but only in his official role, not as a candidate stance on the issue scale's 1–5 questions of how much new funding / what mechanism). Findings: Becerra's only press item in-window is a generic 'closing argument' release on 2026-05-21 with no education or property-tax content; his priorities page still shows the same 8 issues, none education. Porter's in-window press items are two endorsements (SF Chronicle 2026-05-16, Bay Area Reporter 2026-05-13 — the latter just outside window) and an ABC7 interview (2026-05-17) focused on corporate tax, free childcare, free college, $100k income-tax cut, AI, and healthcare — no Prop 13 / property-tax discussion. Thurmond's in-window appearances (KEYT 2026-05-15 profile; May Revise statement 2026-05-14; campaign messaging) remain education-, housing-, affordability-, and immigration-focused with zero water or nuclear content. The 2026-05-14 final debate did not feature Thurmond (tier-2 candidate), and CalMatters / SF Standard / SFist writeups confirm no Prop 13, K-12 funding, nuclear, or water exchanges from Becerra or Porter at that debate either — coverage centered on Becerra's consultant scandal, Chevron donations, AI chatbot regulation, housing, and the hospice-fraud allegations. No CalMatters voter guide update, no new EdSource piece, no AFT/CTA endorsement event for Becerra, no candidate tax-policy interview for Porter, and no post-Fresno-State water follow-up for Thurmond surfaced in the window. All 8 unknowns remain unknown under the project's no-extrapolation rule.
